topic.title: Projects Overview
topic.shortdesc: Contributors have read-only access to the projects they were added to, and work on the content of those projects in a personal workspace.

body.p: A project connects documentation work to a Git repository. As a Contributor, you can work with a project's content, but its owners and maintainers manage the project itself.

section.title: Which Projects You Can See
section.p: The Projects page lists only the projects to which a project owner explicitly added you. This also applies to public projects. Contributors do not automatically get access to the public projects of your organization.

To be added to a project, ask a project owner to add you on the Members page of that project. You are always assigned the Collaborator project role, which is the only project role a Contributor can hold. You receive an email notification when you are added to the project.

section.title: What You Can Do in a Project

ul.li: Browse the project files and read their content.
Edit the project files in your personal workspace.
Suggest your changes to the project team as a review task.
View the project's review tasks and participate in them.

section.p: Your access to project content is read-only. Nothing you do in your personal workspace changes the project until a project maintainer or owner integrates your proposal.

section.title: What Is Not Available
section.p: Contributors cannot access the parts of a project that allow changes affecting everyone. The settings, repository, and deliverables pages, and branch management actions are reserved for project maintainers and owners.
